speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; to begin our evaluation, please describe the onset, progression, and specific nature of your unsteadiness. Additionally, can you list your major past medical conditions and any family history of neurological disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of appearing "drunk" while walking suggests significant incoordination; has this ataxia been present continuously since the onset, or do you experience distinct episodes where your vision blurs or you become confused? Also, you mentioned a significant medical history—could you specify what conditions you have been diagnosed with previously?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The combination of subacute gait and limb ataxia with a history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly suggestive of PML. Given the high suspicion, I am requesting an MRI of the brain to confirm the diagnosis.
